```{ojs}
    const t=document.createElementNS(svgNS,"text");
    t.setAttribute("x",x);t.setAttribute("y",y);t.setAttribute("fill",fill);
    t.setAttribute("font-size",size);t.setAttribute("font-family","sans-serif");
    if(weight)t.setAttribute("font-weight",weight);
    t.textContent=str;s.appendChild(t);
  }
  function mkDot(s,x,y,fill,r){
    const c=document.createElementNS(svgNS,"circle");
    c.setAttribute("cx",x);c.setAttribute("cy",y);c.setAttribute("r",r||"6");
    c.setAttribute("fill",fill);c.setAttribute("stroke","#fff");c.setAttribute("stroke-width","1.5");
    s.appendChild(c);
  }

  // Streamlines Ψ = 2xy = C; for x in [0,2.5], y = C/(2x)
  // Equipotentials Φ = x²-y² = C; parametrise as x = sqrt((C+t²)/2)... or just plot
  function clearSvg(s){while(s.firstChild)s.removeChild(s.firstChild);}

  function render(){
    clearSvg(leftSvg);clearSvg(rightSvg);
    const mode = modeToggle.value;

    // --- LEFT: z-plane, first quadrant ---
    // Solid grey walls (axes)
    const [ox, oy] = ts_fq(0,0);
    mkLine(leftSvg, ox, oy, ts_fq(2.5,0)[0], ts_fq(2.5,0)[1], "#6b7280", 2.5); // x-axis
    mkLine(leftSvg, ox, oy, ts_fq(0,2.2)[0], ts_fq(0,2.2)[1], "#6b7280", 2.5); // y-axis

    // Streamlines Ψ = 2xy = C (blue): y = C/(2x), x in [0.01, 2.5]
    const psiVals = [0.3, 0.7, 1.2, 1.8, 2.5];
    psiVals.forEach(C=>{
      let d="";
      for(let k=1;k<=80;k++){
        const x=0.08+k*2.42/80;
        const y=C/(2*x);
        if(y>2.3)continue;
        const[px,py]=ts_fq(x,y);
        d+=k===1?`M ${px} ${py}`:`L ${px} ${py}`;
      }
      if(d)mkPath(leftSvg,d,mode==="Fluid flow"?"#3b82f6":"#f97316",1.5,mode==="Fluid flow"?null:"4,3");
    });

    // Equipotentials Φ = x²-y² = C (orange dashed): rectangular hyperbolae
    // x² - y² = C; parametrise: x = sqrt(C + y²) for C>0
    const phiVals = [-1.5, -0.8, 0.2, 0.8, 1.5, 2.2];
    phiVals.forEach(C=>{
      let d="";let prev=false;
      for(let k=0;k<=80;k++){
        const y=k*2.3/80;
        const x2=C+y*y;
        if(x2<0.001)continue;
        const x=Math.sqrt(x2);
        if(x>2.5)continue;
        const[px,py]=ts_fq(x,y);
        if(!prev){d=`M ${px} ${py}`;prev=true;}else d+=`L ${px} ${py}`;
      }
      if(d)mkPath(leftSvg,d,mode==="Fluid flow"?"#f97316":"#3b82f6",1.2,"4,3");
    });

    // Tracer dot: moves along streamline Ψ = 1.2, parameterised by angle
    // On streamline 2xy = C: (t/sqrt(2), C/(sqrt(2)*t)) for t in [eps, ...]
    const C_tracer = 1.2;
    const tVal = 0.4 + tracerT * 1.6; // t goes from 0.4 to 2.0
    const tx_z = tVal;
    const ty_z = C_tracer / (2 * tVal);
    if(ty_z > 0 && ty_z < 2.5 && tx_z < 2.5){
      const[dpx,dpy]=ts_fq(tx_z,ty_z);
      mkDot(leftSvg,dpx,dpy,"#fbbf24");
    }

    // Axis labels
    mkTxt(leftSvg,ts_fq(2.4,0)[0]+2,ts_fq(0,0)[1],"Re z","#6b7280","10");
    mkTxt(leftSvg,ts_fq(0,2.1)[0]+4,ts_fq(0,2.1)[1],"Im z","#6b7280","10");
    mkTxt(leftSvg,5,15,"z-plane (first quadrant)","#6b7280","10");

    const wallLabel = mode==="Fluid flow"?"solid walls":"conductor boundaries";
    mkTxt(leftSvg,ox+6,oy-6,wallLabel,"#6b7280","9");

    // --- RIGHT: w-plane, upper half-plane ---
    const WSCALE=40, WCX=WP/2, WCY=HP-20;
    const [wox,woy]=ts_uhp(0,0,WCX,WCY,WSCALE);

    // Real axis (solid wall in w-plane)
    mkLine(rightSvg,10,woy,WP-10,woy,"#6b7280",2.5);

    // w = z² maps: Ψ_w = Im(w) = Im(z²) = 2xy = Ψ_z (same value!)
    // So streamlines Im(w) = C are horizontal lines Im(w) = C
    psiVals.forEach(C=>{
      const [,py]=ts_uhp(0,C,WCX,WCY,WSCALE);
      if(py<5||py>HP-5)return;
      mkLine(rightSvg,10,py,WP-10,py,mode==="Fluid flow"?"#3b82f6":"#f97316",1.5,mode==="Fluid flow"?null:"4,3");
      mkTxt(rightSvg,WP-28,py-3,`Ψ=${C.toFixed(1)}`,"rgba(59,130,246,0.7)","8");
    });

    // Equipotentials Φ_w = Re(w) = Re(z²) = x²-y² = C are vertical lines Re(w) = C
    phiVals.forEach(C=>{
      const[px]=ts_uhp(C,0,WCX,WCY,WSCALE);
      if(px<5||px>WP-5)return;
      mkLine(rightSvg,px,5,px,woy,mode==="Fluid flow"?"#f97316":"#3b82f6",1.2,"4,3");
    });

    // Tracer in w-plane: w = z² for the z-tracer
    const tw_r = tx_z*tx_z - ty_z*ty_z;
    const tw_i = 2*tx_z*ty_z;
    const[wpx,wpy]=ts_uhp(tw_r,tw_i,WCX,WCY,WSCALE);
    if(wpx>5&&wpx<WP-5&&wpy>5&&wpy<woy)mkDot(rightSvg,wpx,wpy,"#fbbf24");

    // Labels
    mkTxt(rightSvg,5,15,"w-plane (upper half-plane)","#6b7280","10");
    mkTxt(rightSvg,WP/2,HP-5,"real axis (boundary)","#6b7280","9","middle");

    // Readout
    const psiLabel = mode==="Fluid flow"?"stream function Ψ":"flux function Ψ";
    const phiLabel = mode==="Fluid flow"?"velocity potential Φ":"electrostatic potential Φ";
    const blueLabel = mode==="Fluid flow"?"streamlines (blue)":"equipotentials (blue)";
    const orangeLabel = mode==="Fluid flow"?"equipotentials (orange dashed)":"field lines (orange dashed)";
    readoutDiv.innerHTML=`<strong>${mode}:</strong> ${blueLabel}: ${psiLabel} = 2xy = C &nbsp;|&nbsp; ${orangeLabel}: ${phiLabel} = x²−y² = C<br>
      <span style="color:#6b7280;font-size:0.9em;">w = z² maps the first-quadrant corner flow to horizontal/vertical uniform flow in the upper half-plane. Both sets of curves are rectangular hyperbolae in z but become straight lines in w.</span>`;
  }

  // Animate tracer along streamline
  function runAnimation(){
    if(animating)return;
    animating=true;tracerT=0;
    const startTime=performance.now(),dur=3000;
    function step(now){
      tracerT=((now-startTime)/dur)%1;
      render();
      animReq=requestAnimationFrame(step);
    }
    animReq=requestAnimationFrame(step);
    // Stop after 3 cycles
    setTimeout(()=>{animating=false;if(animReq)cancelAnimationFrame(animReq);},9000);
  }

  animBtn.addEventListener("input",()=>{if(!animating)runAnimation();});
  modeToggle.addEventListener("input",()=>render());

  render();
  return container;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
katex = require("katex@0.16")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function makeStepperHTML(steps) {
  let current = 0;
  const totalSteps = steps.length;
  const container = document.createElement("div");
  container.style.cssText = "border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem 1.25rem; margin:0.75rem 0; font-family:inherit;";
  const stepsDiv = document.createElement("div");
  stepsDiv.style.marginBottom = "0.75rem";
  function renderSteps() {
    stepsDiv.innerHTML = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < current; i++) {
      const s = steps[i];
      const row = document.createElement("div");
      row.style.cssText = "display:grid; grid-template-columns:220px 1fr; gap:0.35rem 1rem; align-items:baseline; padding:0.35rem 0; border-top:1px solid #f3f4f6;";
      const opCell = document.createElement("span");
      opCell.style.cssText = "font-size:0.85em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
      opCell.textContent = s.op;
      const eqCell = document.createElement("span");
      eqCell.innerHTML = katex.renderToString(s.eq, { throwOnError: false, displayMode: false });
      row.appendChild(opCell); row.appendChild(eqCell);
      if (s.note) {
        const noteRow = document.createElement("div");
        noteRow.style.cssText = "grid-column:2; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; padding-bottom:0.2rem;";
        noteRow.textContent = s.note;
        row.appendChild(noteRow);
      }
      stepsDiv.appendChild(row);
    }
    if (current === totalSteps) {
      const done = document.createElement("div");
      done.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.9em; color:#059669; font-weight:500;";
      done.textContent = "Solution complete.";
      stepsDiv.appendChild(done);
    }
  }
  const controls = document.createElement("div");
  controls.style.cssText = "display:flex; gap:0.5rem; align-items:center;";
  const nextBtn = document.createElement("button");
  nextBtn.textContent = "Next step →";
  nextBtn.style.cssText = "padding:0.42rem 0.95rem; border:1px solid #2563eb; border-radius:5px; background:#2563eb; color:#ffffff; cursor:pointer; font-size:0.9em; font-weight:600; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(37,99,235,0.18);";
  const resetBtn = document.createElement("button");
  resetBtn.textContent = "Reset";
  resetBtn.style.cssText = "padding:0.42rem 0.8rem; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius:5px; background:#f8fafc; cursor:pointer; font-size:0.9em; color:#475569; font-weight:500;";
  const counter = document.createElement("span");
  counter.style.cssText = "font-size:0.82em; color:#9ca3af; margin-left:0.25rem;";
  function updateButtons() {
    nextBtn.disabled = current === totalSteps;
    nextBtn.style.opacity = current === totalSteps ? "0.4" : "1";
    counter.textContent = current === 0 ? "Click to reveal steps" : `Step ${current} of ${totalSteps}`;
  }
  nextBtn.onclick = () => { if (current < totalSteps) { current++; renderSteps(); updateButtons(); } };
  resetBtn.onclick = () => { current = 0; renderSteps(); updateButtons(); };
  controls.appendChild(nextBtn); controls.appendChild(resetBtn); controls.appendChild(counter);
  container.appendChild(stepsDiv); container.appendChild(controls);
  renderSteps(); updateButtons();
  return container;
}
```

### Exercise 1: Image of a circle under $w = z^2$

Find the image of the circle $|z| = 3$ under $w = z^2$. Then find the image of the half-circle $|z| = 3$, $\text{Im}(z) \geq 0$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Parametrise |z| = 3",
    eq: "z = 3e^{i\\theta}, \\quad w = z^2 = 9e^{2i\\theta}"
  },
  {
    op: "Image of full circle",
    eq: "|w| = 9 \\text{ and } \\arg w = 2\\theta \\in [0,4\\pi) \\implies \\text{image is } |w|=9 \\text{ traversed twice}"
  },
  {
    op: "Image of upper half-circle: θ ∈ [0, π]",
    eq: "\\arg w = 2\\theta \\in [0, 2\\pi) \\implies \\text{full circle } |w| = 9 \\text{ traversed once}",
    note: "The upper semicircle maps onto the full circle |w| = 9 — the map w = z² is 2-to-1."
  },
  {
    op: "Critical points check",
    eq: "w'(z) = 2z = 0 \\text{ only at } z=0 \\notin |z|=3 \\implies \\text{map is conformal on the circle}",
    note: "Angles are preserved at every point of the circle."
  }
])
```

### Exercise 2: Image of a strip under $w = e^z$

Find the image of the horizontal strip $\{0 < \text{Im}(z) < \pi/2\}$ under $w = e^z$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Write w = e^{x+iy} = e^x e^{iy}",
    eq: "|w| = e^x \\in (0, \\infty), \\quad \\arg w = y \\in \\left(0, \\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right)"
  },
  {
    op: "Image in the w-plane",
    eq: "\\left\\{w : \\arg w \\in \\left(0, \\tfrac{\\pi}{2}\\right)\\right\\} = \\text{first quadrant of the } w\\text{-plane (excluding axes)}"
  },
  {
    op: "Check boundary images",
    eq: "y=0 \\mapsto \\arg w = 0 \\text{ (positive real axis)};\\quad y=\\pi/2 \\mapsto \\arg w = \\pi/2 \\text{ (positive imaginary axis)}"
  },
  {
    op: "Conformality check: w′(z) = e^z ≠ 0 everywhere",
    eq: "\\text{The map is conformal throughout the strip.}",
    note: "The strip's right angles at its corner (at infinity) map to the right angle at w = 0 in the first quadrant. Conformality is consistent."
  }
])
```

### Exercise 3: Möbius transformation from three point pairs

Find the Möbius transformation mapping $z_1 = 0 \mapsto w_1 = i$, $z_2 = 1 \mapsto w_2 = 0$, $z_3 = -1 \mapsto w_3 = \infty$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "z₃ maps to ∞ means the denominator vanishes at z = −1",
    eq: "w = \\frac{az+b}{c(z+1)} \\quad \\text{(denominator has root at } z=-1\\text{)}"
  },
  {
    op: "Apply w(0) = i",
    eq: "\\frac{b}{c} = i \\implies b = ic"
  },
  {
    op: "Apply w(1) = 0: numerator vanishes at z = 1",
    eq: "a(1) + b = 0 \\implies a = -b = -ic"
  },
  {
    op: "Write the transformation (set c = 1)",
    eq: "w = \\frac{-iz + i}{z + 1} = \\frac{i(1-z)}{z+1}"
  },
  {
    op: "Verify all three pairs",
    eq: "w(0) = i/1 = i\\checkmark, \\quad w(1) = 0/2 = 0\\checkmark, \\quad w(-1) = i(2)/0 = \\infty\\checkmark"
  }
])
```

### Exercise 4: Joukowski map — circle to ellipse

Apply $w = z + 1/z$ to the circle $|z| = 2$. Find the semi-axes of the resulting ellipse.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Parametrise |z| = 2",
    eq: "z = 2e^{i\\theta} \\implies w = 2e^{i\\theta} + \\tfrac{1}{2}e^{-i\\theta}"
  },
  {
    op: "Separate real and imaginary parts",
    eq: "w = \\left(2+\\tfrac{1}{2}\\right)\\cos\\theta + i\\left(2-\\tfrac{1}{2}\\right)\\sin\\theta = \\tfrac{5}{2}\\cos\\theta + i\\tfrac{3}{2}\\sin\\theta"
  },
  {
    op: "Identify as an ellipse",
    eq: "\\frac{(\\text{Re}\\,w)^2}{(5/2)^2} + \\frac{(\\text{Im}\\,w)^2}{(3/2)^2} = \\cos^2\\theta + \\sin^2\\theta = 1"
  },
  {
    op: "Semi-axes",
    eq: "a = \\tfrac{5}{2} = 2.5 \\text{ (horizontal)}, \\quad b = \\tfrac{3}{2} = 1.5 \\text{ (vertical)}",
    note: "General formula for |z| = r: a = r + 1/r, b = r − 1/r. As r → 1⁺, b → 0 and the ellipse collapses to the flat plate [−2, 2]."
  }
])
```

### Exercise 5: Potential theory — flow in a corner

The complex potential $F(w) = w$ represents uniform horizontal flow in the $w$-plane. Apply the conformal map $w = z^2$ to find the complex potential for flow in the first quadrant ($x > 0$, $y > 0$) of the $z$-plane.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Compose: F(z) = F(w)|_{w=z²} = z²",
    eq: "F(z) = z^2 = (x^2-y^2) + 2ixy"
  },
  {
    op: "Identify potential Φ and stream function Ψ",
    eq: "\\Phi = x^2 - y^2 \\text{ (equipotential lines: rectangular hyperbolae)}"
  },
  {
    op: "Stream function",
    eq: "\\Psi = 2xy = \\text{const} \\text{ (streamlines: rectangular hyperbolae } xy = C\\text{)}"
  },
  {
    op: "Verify Φ satisfies Laplace's equation",
    eq: "\\Phi_{xx} + \\Phi_{yy} = 2 + (-2) = 0 \\checkmark"
  },
  {
    op: "Velocity field",
    eq: "\\frac{dF}{dz} = 2z = 2(x+iy) \\implies v_x - iv_y = 2z \\implies v_x = 2x,\\; v_y = -2y",
    note: "Flow moves outward along the x-axis and inward along the y-axis — the stagnation-point flow pattern seen in a jet impinging on a flat plate."
  }
])
```

With these four chapters you have the core analytic methods: complex differentiation and the Cauchy-Riemann equations, contour integration and Cauchy's theorem, Laurent series and residues, and conformal mapping. They connect directly to the rest of engineering mathematics — the Laplace equation in any two-dimensional domain, potential flow around aerofoils, inverse Laplace transforms via residues, and stability analysis in the complex frequency plane.

- [NOTE] The standard mapping $w = (z-i)/(z+i)$ (upper half-plane → unit disk) is correctly stated. The inverse direction (unit disk → upper half-plane) uses $z = i(1-w)/(1+w)$, which is not given — no issue since the chapter doesn't claim to list inverses, but worth noting for completeness.

## Chapter 04 — Conformal mapping

### Fixes applied
- [WARN FIXED] Complex potential section: added the missing word "incompressible" to the flow description. A stream function exists only for incompressible flow; irrotationality alone is insufficient. The complex potential F = Φ + iΨ requires ∇·v = 0 (stream function) AND ∇×v = 0 (velocity potential) simultaneously. The omission could mislead students applying this to compressible flows.
- [NOTE FIXED] Complex velocity convention ($dF/dz = v_x - iv_y$) has been moved from Exercise 5 notes into the body text (§ Complex potential), where engineers need it when first encountering the complex potential. The exercise note still references it for the worked example.

### Open issues
- [NOTE] The `eng` destinations hook (Joukowski transformation, thin-aerofoil theory) is accurate and well-placed. Joukowski aerofoils were historically important (early 20th-century aircraft) and the transform is still taught in aerodynamics courses (e.g. NACA thin-aerofoil theory builds on this framework).
- [NOTE] "Kutta-Joukowski's theorem" in the body text — standard English usage is "Kutta–Joukowski theorem" (em-dash or hyphen, no possessive 's'). Math-prof flagged this. From an engineering credibility standpoint the possessive form is unusual and slightly odd; recommend correcting to "Kutta–Joukowski theorem".
- [NOTE] The formula $L = \rho U \Gamma$ (lift per unit span) is dimensionally consistent: $[\text{kg/m}^3 \cdot \text{m/s} \cdot \text{m}^2\text{/s}] = [\text{N/m}]$. Correct.
- [NOTE] `destinations.sci.hook` — "Conformal mapping solves the two-dimensional Laplace equation — electrostatics, magnetostatics, and heat conduction in irregular geometries." Accurate. These are the canonical engineering/science applications.
- [NOTE] `destinations.comp.hook` — "Schwarz-Christoffel formula ... used in numerical PDE solvers and in computer graphics for texture mapping on curved surfaces." Accurate. The SC Toolbox (Driscoll & Trefethen) is widely used in numerical conformal mapping for FEM mesh generation and BVP solvers.
- [NOTE] `stroud_programme: null` — Stroud touches conformal mapping briefly; Kreyszig Ch 17 is the primary reference here. The null is defensible given Stroud's limited coverage, but worth confirming.

<!-- STUDENT REVIEW
## Chapter 04 — Conformal mapping
Layer: engineering

### Confusion points

1. **Angle-preservation argument relies on complex multiplication = rotation, which isn't stated** (§ Conformal mappings, "Why angles are preserved"). The key step — that multiplying the tangent vector by f′(z₀) rotates it by arg f′(z₀) — is compressed to "follows from the chain rule." A reader who is not comfortable seeing complex multiplication as a rotation will not close this gap unaided.

2. **"A line is a circle through ∞"** (§ Möbius transformations). The extended complex plane (Riemann sphere, point at infinity) has not been introduced. Using it without definition asks the reader to accept a surprising-sounding claim on authority.

3. **Cross-ratio: no indication of how to use it** (§ Three-point determination). The formula is given but the procedure — set the two cross-ratios equal, solve the resulting linear equation in w — is not stated. A reader will not know whether to expand, factorise, or use some other technique.

4. **Circulation Γ undefined** (§ Joukowski transformation, "Why it works"). The Kutta-Joukowski lift formula contains Γ without definition. An engineering student who hasn't taken fluid mechanics won't know what circulation is. This is the chapter's headline engineering result; the audience deserves to know what Γ means.

5. **Composed potential notation is ambiguous** (§ Application to potential theory, worked example). "F(w) = w maps to F(z) = f(z)" conflates the function F and its argument. The correct statement is that the composed potential is F(f(z)) = f(z) = z², but the notation used can be read as F(z) being a different object from F(w).

### Reassurance gaps

- The standard mappings (§ Standard conformal maps) list three maps and describe their domain/image pairs but give no worked verification. An engineering reader wants to confirm they can reproduce the w = e^z strip result before moving on. Exercise 2 covers this, but a brief check in the body — "confirm the boundary y=0 maps to the positive real axis: e^{x+0i} = e^x > 0 ✓" — would reduce anxiety.

- After the Joukowski section, a reader is likely to ask: "could I compute the lift on a specific aerofoil using this?" The answer (in principle, yes, by computing the residue of the complex velocity) is not given, and the chapter ends without making clear what the reader could now do that they couldn't before.

### Exercise calibration

- Exercise 3 (Möbius transformation from three point pairs) is a well-matched engineering-layer exercise with a concrete procedure.
- Exercise 5 (potential theory — flow in a corner) is the most conceptually demanding and requires understanding all three threads: conformality, complex potential, and the Cauchy-Riemann connection. It is well-constructed but is significantly harder than Exercises 1–2.
- The jump from Exercise 4 (Joukowski circle → ellipse, essentially mechanical substitution) to Exercise 5 (potential theory) is steep. Exercises 1–4 feel computational; Exercise 5 requires synthesis. Some readers will stall here.
- All exercises have clean, satisfying answers. The variety across exercises is good.

### Wayfinding

- `opens_to` points to "Vector integral calculus" with relationship `enriches`. This is the first chapter in the series where `opens_to` leaves the complex-analysis section entirely. The reader is not told this — no sentence signals "this is where complex analysis connects back into the rest of engineering mathematics." A closing remark noting what the reader has now equipped themselves to tackle (potential theory, the Laplace equation in any 2D domain, thin-aerofoil calculations) would be a strong finish.

## Verdict: READABLE WITH FIXES

The chapter is accessible and the Joukowski content is genuinely motivating. The main friction points are: the unexplained circulation Γ (a gap in an otherwise excellent engineering hook), the opaque cross-ratio usage instructions, and the "line is a circle through ∞" assertion that rests on an unintroduced concept. The potential-theory section is the weakest in terms of notation clarity and benefits from a minor rewrite of the worked example.
-->
